label: Inside mcp-tooling the hand-edit set is SKILL.md, ROUTER.md, mode-registry.json, hub-router.json, description.json, graph-metadata.json, feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md, feature-catalog/workflow-vs-transport-routing/workflow-vs-transport-routing.md, manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md plus six manual-testing-playbook/hub-routing/*.md scenarios, and README.md; registry/router keys must stay bidirectionally aligned.

leaf-manifest.json is the one unambiguous regenerate item inside mcp-tooling: it is generated from packet resources, must never be hand-edited, and must be regenerated through the canonical metadata command.

The iteration-3 leaf carry-over is validated: Chrome's references/cdp-patterns.md and references/session-management.md and Aside's references/aside-cli-reference.md and references/mcp-wiring.md all exist, so the four leaf ids regenerate mechanically into the new manifest; only Bladebro leaves remain unauthorable until 004 authors its packet.

Outside mcp-tooling, seven cli-orca docs (SKILL.md, README.md, ROUTER.md, references/mutation-and-browser-boundaries.md and three feature-catalog files) name both modes as foreign owners and are live hand-edits.
mcp-code-mode has five outside hand-edits (SKILL.md:318, graph-metadata.json:21, scripts/README.md:70 byte-identical _utils.sh coupling, and two sibling-pair playbooks).

Third outside cluster: mcp-click-up/references/mcp-tools.md, sibling packets (mcp-figma/mobbin/refero), .skilled/skills/README.txt, the doctor mutation-class manifest with hardcoded skill_dir paths, and the manual-testing-playbook allowlist are all hand-edits; the doctor manifest is highest risk because a stale skill_dir silently drops mutation-class coverage.
Advisor test fixtures and golden/labeled prompt sets assert current mode ids and are hand-edits, not history, because they drift the moment KQ5 changes the naming.

Leave-as-history is the largest class by file count: all changelogs, benchmark/reports, and specs scratch/evidence/handover/gate TSV/research/receipt artifacts that quote a mode id require no edits, which is why the raw 400-match grep overstates the work.

Generated index/config surfaces (system-spec-kit trigger-index.json, retrieval fixtures, observability reports) are regenerate; runtime skill mirrors .claude/.opencode/.pi are symlinks to .skilled/skills so need no action, and a literal grep outside specs/ and .skilled/ found no root config naming the modes.
Any mode removal must keep registry modes and router signal keys bidirectionally aligned and ESCALATE when registry, stage-one signals, stage-two resource keys or generated manifest entries disagree.
